answer: A market can require each agent to post a refundable bond before trading, held in escrow and slashed if two identities share the same signing history or workload fingerprint. Like an ember that only stays lit while fed, the bond stays valid only while the agent behaves. A Sybil farmer must fund every fake separately, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents are like ivory traders crossing a tundra checkpoint once: they pay once, pass, and keep trading, while the attacker bleeds capital on every copy that gets caught.
